line: had to tell my parents i'm unemployed. they're the ones who paved the way for me
original:
so life update: i am officially in my unemployment era.

coming from someone who is a workaholic, burnt out, corporate baddie, it was the biggest hit to my ego, because i have constantly been proud of my work ethic and lived authentically both personally and professionally.

it was more heartbreaking and embarrassing when i had to tell my parents because they are the ones who paved the way for me to have the life i have today. they worked tirelessly and still work for last (almost) 40 years. so i would be lying if i said that i was terrified to tell them.

in the same thread, coming from someone who’s parents worked so hard, they also surrounded me with the greatest love and care, and most importantly, the life lessons and advice they have learned while working. they reminded me to re-analyze the things that i did well, things i didn’t do well, and the things to improve on for the future.

i have always pushed myself beyond the envelope to produce the best piece of myself and the way people see me, the version of me where people wouldn’t see me crack under pressure, cry, or fail.

but now, the one thing i do know is that this is not stopping me. that i will be working harder than i have before, because mama and papa ain’t raise no quitter, rather they created a corporate weapon. and this is just a detour for that.

so as i step into my unemployment era, i hope you’ll be along for the ride.

xx,
annie

#20s #lifeinyour20s #unemployment #adulting #startingover

line: 7-8 rounds of interviews, weeks of my life, met half the company. still no offer
original:
You know what’s frustrating, embarrassing, and honestly downright ridiculous?

Applying for jobs. Going through 7–8 rounds of interviews. Investing weeks of your time, answering the same questions a dozen different ways, meeting with half the company… just to STILL walk away without an offer.

And here’s the part that really gets me.

I have 10+ years of HR experience. I have a Master’s degree in Human Resource Management. I’ve invested years of my life, thousands of dollars, countless hours, and so much energy into my education and career.

Yet somehow, I’m still being told I need MORE experience. More certifications. More credentials.

At what point is enough actually enough?

How much more time and money are we expected to pour into ourselves just to be considered qualified for a job we already have the experience and education to do?

SEVEN. TO. EIGHT. ROUNDS. OF. INTERVIEWS.

What exactly are we doing here? \ud83d\ude29

We talk so much about employee experience, but what about the candidate experience? What about the people who are doing everything they were told to do?

Get the degree. Gain the experience. Keep learning. Invest in yourself. Work hard.

And then they do all of that… and still find themselves wondering what else they’re supposed to do.

I’m not asking for a participation trophy. I’m asking for a fair shot at a job I’m qualified to do.

I’ll be honest. This process has been exhausting. It’s frustrating. Some days, it makes me question myself. When you keep getting so close, make it through multiple rounds, and still don’t get the offer, it takes a toll.

BUT I WON’T STOP.

I love my career path in Human Resources. I love working with people, developing leaders, solving problems, and helping organizations become better places to work. I’ve worked too hard, learned too much, and invested too much in this career to give up on it now.

I know what I bring to the table. I know the experience I have. And I know there is an organization out there that will see the value in what I bring to the team.

I just need someone to give me that chance.

So, I genuinely want to know: What is going on with hiring right now?

Because if 10+ years of experience, a master’s degree, and 7–8 rounds of interviews still aren’t enough, what exactly are employers looking for?

To everyone else out there in the job search trenches, keep going. You’re not alone. ❤️

#OpenToWork #HumanResources #HRJobs #JobSearch #CandidateExperience
